rationale: Evidence: 0 of 120 development trials finished across iterations 0 and 1. Every run went off track at progress 0.10 to 0.15, and max_error reached about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is 0.06 m for any allowed body width). Score is therefore driven almost entirely by how far the robot gets before it leaves the tape. Iteration 0 (score 53.0) beat iteration 1 (score 50.6). Iteration 1 changed several things at once (wider and forward sensors, kp 4.5, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.3, narrower track and lower mass), so I cannot attribute its loss to any one change. The s-bend progress was identical (0.1475) in both iterations, which suggests a fixed failure point, probably an early sharp bend or the start. Line loss happened about once per run, so the robot loses the tape at that point and does not recover. Changes from iteration 0: (1) sensor_size raised from 0.012 to 0.016 m, so each sensor covers more of the 25 mm tape and keeps a reading through the bend, which should reduce line-loss events. (2) Sensors kept at the iteration 0 geometry (x = +/-0.04, +/-0.02, 0; y = 0.04), so the comparison with iteration 0 stays clean. (3) kp raised from 3.0 to 4.5 for a stronger correction on drift, with kd raised from 0.5 to 1.0 to damp it. (4) ki lowered to 0.02 to avoid windup on bends. (5) base_speed lowered from 1.6 to 1.5, a small cut to give the controller more time at bends while staying near the speed needed for a 3 s finish. Geometry and drivetrain otherwise match iteration 0. Expected result: progress somewhat above 0.15 and fewer line-loss events, so a score modestly above 53. Completion is still unlikely, because the robot is not yet tracking well enough to cover the full course.
